events.did: served a pretty girl an iced latte and told her she had picked her own eyes
events.quote_anchor: June smiled. “Aw, thanks!” she said. “I picked them out myself.”

events.did: grazed rude customers' fingers when handing off their order, in case she ever needed a disposable corpse
events.quote_anchor: whenever someone was a dick, she made sure to graze their fingers when she handed off their order

events.did: swept a hand over the table by the machines and demanded to know what the mess was
events.quote_anchor: “What the hell is this?” he asked, sweeping a hand over the table by the machines, cluttered with wrong orders and ruined drinks.

events.did: blamed the machine for the mess and batted her blue eyes until Max flushed red
events.quote_anchor: She batted her blue eyes. They were really pretty. Max flushed red, and said it was fine.

events.did: grabbed a macchiato order for Jeff and ducked under the counter to go on break
events.quote_anchor: June grabbed one of the to-go cups from the collection of messed-up orders—a macchiato for someone named Jeff—and ducked under the counter.

events.did: locked Ava in a very nice house in the woods with plenty of supplies so her power would keep working
events.quote_anchor: June had still tried, opting for the latter, locking a woman—whose name was Ava—in a very nice house in the woods, with plenty of supplies.

events.did: woke in the middle of the night back in her own body, side on fire, the borrowed shape suddenly gone
events.quote_anchor: Only to wake up in the middle of the night back in her own body, side on fire, the shape she’d chosen suddenly gone.

events.did: opened an encrypted app and answered a listing, and felt her spirits lift
events.quote_anchor: She answered the listing, and felt her spirits lift, her focus sharpen.

relations.did: texted June once a month since she went dark, sending only her name followed by a question mark
relations.quote_anchor: He’d messaged her once a month since she went dark, the texts all brief, nothing but her name followed by a question mark.

relations.did: kept her only connection to Syd instead of getting a new phone
relations.quote_anchor: the thought of losing her only connection to Syd had stopped her

relations.did: stashed the original owner of her borrowed body, Ava, in a house in the woods
relations.quote_anchor: locking a woman—whose name was Ava—in a very nice house in the woods

relations.did: calls himself the manager of the coffee shop where June works
relations.quote_anchor: “May!” hollered an acne-ridden boy named Max who called himself the manager.

numbers.did: almost a year before (how long ago she had been shot, so the wound was still fresh)
numbers.quote_anchor: even though she’d been shot almost a year before, the gunshot wound was still fresh

numbers.did: nearly two months (how long she kept the life she built from scratch)
numbers.quote_anchor: It seemed a better plan, and she’d gotten nearly two months in, long enough to make friends, get a job, have the beginnings of a life.

numbers.did: once a month (how often he messaged June while she was dark)
numbers.quote_anchor: He’d messaged her once a month since she went dark

numbers.did: a few days (how long she had been working at the coffee shop)
numbers.quote_anchor: She’d only been there a few days, but it was good people-watching

numbers.did: For years (how long she had wondered what her life would have been if she had stayed human)
numbers.quote_anchor: For years she’d wondered who she might have been, without that cataclysmic crossroads, what kind of life she would have lived, if she’d stayed human.
